currentContext.business: HCLTech brings together technology and its people to supercharge progress for clients, serving Global 2000 enterprises as a preferred digital transformation partner. Its portfolio spans engineering, digital, cloud, AI and software, including a full-stack AI solutions portfolio built to accelerate enterprise AI adoption - AI Advisory, AI Engineering (Physical AI and Kinetic AI robotics/automation), AI Factory cognitive infrastructure and Sovereign AI - alongside differentiated IP and repeatable solutions across IT, SDLC, engineering and BPO services and the HCLSoftware products business. Delivery runs through a global network spanning 60 countries and deep partnerships with leading hyperscalers and technology OEMs, enabling clients to deploy cutting-edge digital technologies at speed and scale.

AI solutions portfolio: AI Force (flagship AI platform, deployed across 75 clients)
VisionX (multimodal AI solution for physical operations)
AI Advisory (AI consulting from blueprint to POCs to responsible deployment)
AI Engineering (Physical AI; Kinetic AI for robotics and automation)
AI Factory (AI data center design, build and operate services)
Sovereign AI (self-controlled AI infrastructure, data and models for regulated enterprises and governments)
Internal enterprise platforms: LUMI (enterprise AI agent for instant resolution of employee queries)

currentContext.expansion: HCLTech is asset-light - it does not produce physical products or own/operate any manufacturing facilities - and the routed sections disclose no plant, capacity or rupee capex programme. FY 2025-26 expansion was capability-, footprint- and entity-led. Capability build-out centres on the AI portfolio: AI Factory, described as comprehensive cognitive infrastructure spanning AI data center design, build and operate services; AI Engineering covering Physical AI (embedding intelligence into physical systems and environments) and Kinetic AI (robotics and automation); AI Advisory; and Sovereign AI for governments and heavily regulated sectors that want AI developed, deployed and governed on infrastructure, data and models controlled entirely within their firms. The flagship AI Force platform is now deployed across 75 clients, VisionX addresses multimodal AI for physical operations, and internal deployments include LUMI and Talent Navigator; capacity for this build-out was created by training over 144,000 employees in GenAI in FY26, including 11,800 certified AI Builders and more than 700 certified blackbelts. Footprint expansion came through two new step-down wholly owned subsidiaries - HCL Technologies Holdings GmbH under the laws of Austria and HCL Technologies Middle East LLC under the laws of the UAE - on top of a delivery network already spanning 60 countries. Inorganically, Actian Germany GmbH acquired Wobby BV of Belgium, an Agentic AI software startup providing AI Data Analyst 'Agents' for data warehouses, and HCL Singapore Pte Ltd acquired Finergic Solutions Pte. Ltd. of Singapore, which provides core banking and wealth management transformation programs; completion on March 6, 2026 also brought Finergic Consulting Pte. Ltd. (Singapore) and Finergic Luxembourg S.A. (Luxembourg) in as step-down wholly owned subsidiaries. Running the other way, the Company pursued deliberate entity rationalisation to optimise resources and manage costs, merging or closing five entities during the year - Zeenea Benelux voluntarily liquidated on April 10, 2025; Geometric China, Inc. de-registered on September 24, 2025; the CeleritiFinTech Limited joint venture liquidated on October 28, 2025; Actian International Inc. merged into Actian Corporation on December 1, 2025; and Confinale (UK) Limited voluntarily dissolved on January 27, 2026. On funding, HCL America Inc. fully repaid the balance outstanding USD 252.207 million of 1.375% senior unsecured notes on March 10, 2026, after which the Trustee released the Company's guarantee and no Notes remain outstanding. The Board recorded no material changes or commitments affecting the financial position of the Company between the end of the financial year and the date of the Report.
currentContext.mdna: FY26 was a muted demand environment - cautious technology services spending, macro-economic uncertainty and geopolitical volatility tested resilience.|AI and adjacent technologies are seen as a powerful tailwind that will open larger opportunities and accelerate growth, with the technology industry undergoing a tectonic shift as AI reshapes how work gets done.|AI is creating enormous opportunities through entirely new business propositions even as it quietly reshapes much of the old; the companies that define the next decade will do both.|Advanced AI revenue of $620 million at year end is presented as the measure of a fast-maturing AI play and of the ability to offset AI-led deflation with new revenue streams.|Peer-leading constant currency growth for a third consecutive year is attributed to the differentiated portfolio, the ability to execute at scale and the commitment of people.|Sector sentiment has been cautious and near-term prices do not always reflect the fundamentals being built, while the underlying health of the business remains strong.|Management expects this AI cycle to be the most transformative and rewarding of the disruptions the industry has been through, and remains fully invested in the growth strategy.|The underlying health of the business, be it the order book, client relationships and deal pipeline, remains strong.

risks.risk: People-dependent delivery model exposed to attrition and wage/skill inflation
risks.note: The BRSR reports a workforce of 237,098 (227,181 permanent) and voluntary attrition (LTM - IT Services) of 12.51% for permanent employees in FY26 against 12.99% in FY25 and 12.42% in FY24. HCLTech owns no plants or manufacturing facilities, so capacity is entirely people; sustained double-digit churn in a business selling billable skills is a structural cost and delivery-continuity risk, aggravated by the need to re-skill the base for AI, automation, cybersecurity and cloud.

risks.risk: Revenue concentrated in a single business activity and one dominant segment
risks.note: 100% of turnover comes from one activity - computer programming, consultancy, software and related activities (GICS Information Technology - Software and Services). Within that, IT & Business Services contributes 74% of turnover, Engineering and R&D Services 17% and HCLSoftware 9%. There is no diversifying business line, so any downturn in enterprise IT services demand or in the ITBS segment flows almost fully to the top line.

risks.risk: Export and currency concentration - over nine-tenths of standalone turnover is exported
risks.note: The BRSR states exports contribute 91.54% of total turnover for the standalone entity, with markets across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. Revenue is therefore earned largely in foreign currency against a substantially INR/offshore cost base, exposing reported earnings to exchange-rate movement and to demand, immigration and trade policy in a small number of overseas markets.

risks.risk: Client concentration in a narrow set of very large enterprise accounts
risks.note: The Company positions itself as a preferred digital and AI partner to Global 2000 companies, Global 2000 equivalent organizations and emerging enterprises, and states that its strategy 'emphasizes building deep, strategic client relationships as a trusted long-term partner'. That deep-few model concentrates revenue in large accounts, so the loss, insourcing or budget cut of a top relationship is disproportionately material.

risks.risk: Exposure to heavily regulated client verticals and their compliance regimes
risks.note: Clients are concentrated in Financial Services, Manufacturing, Life Sciences and Healthcare, Technology and Services, Public Services (Energy & Utilities, Travel-Transport-Logistics and Government), Retail and CPG, and Telecommunications, Media, Publishing and Entertainment. Serving regulated and government customers imports their data-protection, security and procurement obligations into HCLTech's delivery, raising the cost of failure on any engagement.

As on March 31, 2026 the Company had 125 subsidiaries and 3 associate companies, with new entities incorporated in Austria (HCL Technologies Holdings GmbH) and the UAE (HCL Technologies Middle East LLC) during the year. The Directors' Report acknowledges the burden directly, noting that restructuring is done 'after taking into consideration the business aspects, local laws and regulations' in order to reduce the number of entities - i.e. a standing compliance, tax and administrative-cost overhead across many jurisdictions.

risks.risk: Acquisition, integration and portfolio-churn execution risk
risks.note: FY26 saw two acquisitions (Wobby BV, an Agentic AI software startup in Belgium, via Actian Germany GmbH; and Finergic Solutions Pte. Ltd. of Singapore, core banking and wealth-management transformation, via HCL Singapore Pte Ltd, completed March 6, 2026, pulling in Finergic Consulting Pte. Ltd. and Finergic Luxembourg S.A.) alongside five entities merged, liquidated or de-registered - including the liquidation of the CeleritiFinTech Limited joint venture on October 28, 2025. Continuous inorganic capability-buying and entity unwinding carries integration, retention and value-realisation risk.

risks.risk: Reliance on the internal control, ethics and risk-policy framework rather than a disclosed enterprise risk register
risks.note: Risk oversight rests on a Board Risk Management Committee (one of six Board Committees), a Risk Management Policy 'that ensures appropriate management of risks in line with its internal systems and culture', and internal financial controls designed for 'safeguarding of assets from unauthorized use & prevention and detection of frauds & errors'. The Directors' Report itself carries no risk enumeration - it defers the detailed Risk Management section to the MD&A - so investors depend on the effectiveness of that framework, and on the auditors' clean report and no-fraud statement, for assurance.

one-line thesis: HCLTech opened FY27 with a seasonally-weak-but-resilient Q1 (revenue $3,650M, −0.5% QoQ / +2.6% YoY CC; margin 16.9%, +39bps QoQ) carried by record Q1 bookings ($2.4B net-new TCV, highest-ever Q1) and Advanced AI ($171M, +62% YoY). The headline event is a strategic pivot into the AI-datacenter/full-stack sovereign-AI business — an initial INR3,500cr investment scaling toward a 50MW ambition — funded off FCF/partners without touching the 75%+ payout policy. FY27 guidance held at 1–4% CC / 17.5–18.5% EBIT despite two US-telco discretionary cuts and a structural healthcare-vertical drag.

Fortune 250 semiconductor-equipment OEM: SAP-enabled design-to-manufacturing, SAP + PLM + MES integration.

segment / subsidiary detail: ITBS: flat QoQ, +4.2% YoY — resilient despite two-telco headwind + SAP program.
ERS: −3.7% QoQ, +0.3% YoY — decline concentrated in Tech and Telecom, Media & Entertainment; sharp discretionary cuts in two large US telcos + high tech base.

HCL Software: $313M, +2.2% QoQ / −5.3% YoY; ARR $1.063B (+2% YoY). Jaspersoft adds the visualization layer to data portfolio (DataConnect, Ingres, Informix, Zen, VectorAI DB, Data Intelligence/Observability).
Verticals: 6 of 7 grew YoY; led by Public Services +12% and Retail & CPG +10.1%; BFSI strong (~12 quarters of momentum, highest-in-industry YoY). Weak: Telecom, High-tech, Life Sciences/Healthcare.
Clients added (YoY): +1 in $100M, +6 in $50M, +11 in $20M, +31 in $10M.
People: 223,889 (−3,292 QoQ); attrition 12.7% LTM; revenue/employee +3.3% YoY (up 5 straight quarters).
growth verticals / optionality: AI-native + AI-amplified services: fastest-growing enterprise-spend pool — the intended disproportionate beneficiary; AI-disrupted (commoditized) work to be optimised/deflated faster than the market.
AI Datacenter business (NEW growth vector) — see §8. Full-stack (design + DevOps + cloud ops + software), not colo; anchors managed-services / outcome-based contracts.

Sovereign AI-as-a-service / SLMs: zero-trust + tiered architecture (Tier-1 private on-prem/VPC SLMs fine-tuned on enterprise data; Tier-2 frontier models via policy-enforcing inferencing gateway). $150M strategic investment in Sarvam opens Indian sovereign-AI market; SLM-training = "another engineering-services wave."
AI IP / platforms: AI Force 2.2 (VS Code plugin, multimodal, long-term memory, AWS-native), Agent Store, AI Force for Oracle; deployed across 92 client accounts; 23 industry AI solutions.

Partnerships: Red Hat (AI Factory), Google Cloud (dedicated Gemini enterprise BU + autonomous finance platform), Intel + Google Cloud AI Innovation Zones (Santa Clara, Chennai), OpenAI Trusted Access for Cyber, AWS AI Services Competency, Dell/HPE partner-of-the-year, MetLife Stadium AI partner (FIFA 2026 final venue).
margins & cost dynamics: Reported EBIT margin walk QoQ (JFM'26 16.5% → AMJ'26 16.9%, +39bps): +70bps lower restructuring, +20bps PDD benefit, +60bps forex; −110bps seasonality (annual productivity give-backs + ERS decline).
Restructuring 62bps drag in Q1; ex-restructuring margin 17.5% (vs 17.7% prior Q).

Guidance embeds ~40–50bps restructuring cost for FY27. Strategy = "superior growth at stable margins"; won't compromise mega-deal margins (risk-management/execution rigor). Gross margin/employee expected to rise with revenue/employee, but mgmt "will not hesitate to invest" through the AI inflection.
capex / expansion (watch slippage) — ai: Entering the AI-datacenter business: strategic investment of up to INR3,500 crore (initial), with a long-term ambition to scale to 50MW of capacity.

INR3,500cr is NOT the cost of 50MW — mgmt explicit: it funds "a fraction of that capacity" to get started; 50MW is the long-term vision. Full-stack 50MW at ~$60–80B/GW math implies ~INR30,000cr, but mgmt "don't expect to be anywhere near INR30,000cr."

Funding: won't sit entirely on balance sheet in one year; mix of partners (silicon/OEM vendors), committed client capacity, GPUs financed against contracted demand, and equity+debt. Explicitly not at the expense of the payout policy.

Full-stack, not colo: "megawatt isn't the product, it's the anchor" — value is high-margin AI services (SLM-led, industry/vertical models) wrapped around capacity; drives outcome-based + managed-services contracts (some capacity consumed internally).

Demand backdrop: global DC demand to triple by 2030 (AI ~70% of growth), India even faster + one of the most supply-constrained DC markets; sovereign-data mandates require in-country workloads. Market "heavily GPU-starved… no ambiguity."
Client commitment: in advanced discussions to secure committed consumption "from day one." Next-tranche investment gated on delivery of the initial investment (disciplined, FCF-linked).
Note: separate $150M strategic investment in Sarvam (sovereign-AI stack) — distinct from the DC capex.
capital allocation: Interim dividend INR12/share (record date 17-Jul-26, pay 27-Jul-26); LTM dividend INR60/share = 93.2% payout of net income. (Prior-year board policy: return ≥75% of net income.)
AI-datacenter capex explicitly ring-fenced from the payout policy; funded via FCF + partner/debt mix, disciplined and staged.
Acquisitions: Jaspersoft (completed), CTG (pending), Sarvam ($150M strategic stake).
risks & watch-items: Two large US telcos — sharp discretionary-spend cuts; already flagged last quarter, now playing through ERS (Tech/Telecom/Media) in subsequent quarters.

Healthcare / Life Sciences — structural drag: off a ~$500M run-rate, gradual decline over 8–9 quarters; medical-device regulatory work ended and wasn't refilled; US healthcare sector "heavily stressed" (most of the vertical's revenue is US).

AI price deflation — AI-disrupted/commoditised services being optimised away; TCV-per-deal pressure; token-cost economics (costs may fall but total token consumption/cost rises → need economic tiered/SLM model).

Datacenter execution / tenancy risk — analyst pushback on ROIC/tenancy if the compute-demand cycle turns (100GW of announced AI-DC pipeline; SpaceX/Meta leasing compute); mgmt counters market is "heavily GPU-starved," 50MW is a tiny fraction of need.
Guidance conservatism — held 1–4% despite record bookings; macro unchanged since March; directional update only after Q2.
New Labor Code one-time EPS impact; DSO up 2 days.
management quality / tone: Confident and specific on AI strategy (five pillars, named deals, hard AI-revenue numbers); disciplined on capital ("won't correlate INR3,500cr with 50MW," FCF-gated, payout-protected).
Transparent on idiosyncratic weakness (named two-telco cuts, healthcare structural drag) rather than glossing.
Pragmatic on guidance — deliberately conservative given only one quarter in and unchanged macro; measured on mega-deal contribution timing (Apr-2027 steady state).
non-obvious takeaways: The AI-datacenter move is a business-model inflection — a services company building infrastructure, which mgmt frames as a reversal of the cloud/digital cycle (then you partnered hyperscalers; now private/sovereign SLM stacks require owning the full stack). Watch capital discipline vs. scope creep toward 50MW.
"Megawatt is the anchor, not the product" — the DC play is really a wrapper to lock in high-margin managed-services/outcome-based contracts and internal consumption, not a colo/capacity land-grab.
Sovereign-AI/SLM thesis reframes AI deflation as an engineering-services tailwind (data work + model training per client) rather than a pure headwind.
Record Q1 bookings + a separately-announced mega deal, yet guidance untouched — signals mgmt sees near-term revenue governed by seasonality/give-backs and the telco/healthcare drag, not order intake.

guidance (critical — verify next quarter: FY27 revenue growth: retained 1–4% CC — organic, excludes acquisitions (incl. Jaspersoft, CTG).
FY27 EBIT margin: 17.5–18.5% — organic; includes ~40–50bps restructuring-cost impact. Acquisition revenue/margin sits on top of (outside) the guide.
Guidance held despite record Q1 bookings — mgmt wants to "see how things pan out next quarter"; will revisit directional change after Q2.
Mega deal (Fortune Global 50, Europe) signed early July → NOT in Q1; transition starts in ~2 months, steady state only Apr-2027 → negligible FY27 revenue impact.
Jaspersoft: ~$10–15M/quarter contribution from Q2 (seasonality-affected), outside guidance.
CTG: expected to close later part of this (Q2) quarter, outside guidance.
Margin recovery to old 18–19% band: deferred — will give FY28 guidance "at an appropriate time" next year.
order book & pipeline: Net-new TCV $2.4B, "highest-ever Q1 bookings"; well-balanced across verticals / service lines / geographies. Excludes the July mega deal.

Mega deal (post-Q1): Europe-HQ Fortune Global 50 firm — technology partner for AI-led transformation of digital workplace + enterprise networks (AI Force platform, software-defined solutions, digital employee experience).
AI Factory: global technology major expanded partnership, incremental scope >$180M for AI datacenter build-out (latest GPU tech, LLM training).
Fortune 250 semiconductor-equipment OEM: SAP-enabled design-to-manufacturing, SAP + PLM + MES integration.
Europe automotive OEM: AI-led SRE transformation (AI Force). Europe manufacturer: physical-AI navigation stack for autonomous robot. Indian research org: secure chip / trusted-computing silicon.
Pipeline described "healthy"; encouraged by potential Q2 bookings. AI Labs crossed 1,000+ AI engagements in Q1.
segment / subsidiary detail: ITBS: flat QoQ, +4.2% YoY — resilient despite two-telco headwind + SAP program.
ERS: −3.7% QoQ, +0.3% YoY — decline concentrated in Tech and Telecom, Media & Entertainment; sharp discretionary cuts in two large US telcos + high tech base.

HCL Software: $313M, +2.2% QoQ / −5.3% YoY; ARR $1.063B (+2% YoY). Jaspersoft adds the visualization layer to data portfolio (DataConnect, Ingres, Informix, Zen, VectorAI DB, Data Intelligence/Observability).
Verticals: 6 of 7 grew YoY; led by Public Services +12% and Retail & CPG +10.1%; BFSI strong (~12 quarters of momentum, highest-in-industry YoY). Weak: Telecom, High-tech, Life Sciences/Healthcare.
Clients added (YoY): +1 in $100M, +6 in $50M, +11 in $20M, +31 in $10M.
People: 223,889 (−3,292 QoQ); attrition 12.7% LTM; revenue/employee +3.3% YoY (up 5 straight quarters).
growth verticals / optionality: AI-native + AI-amplified services: fastest-growing enterprise-spend pool — the intended disproportionate beneficiary; AI-disrupted (commoditized) work to be optimised/deflated faster than the market.
AI Datacenter business (NEW growth vector) — see §8. Full-stack (design + DevOps + cloud ops + software), not colo; anchors managed-services / outcome-based contracts.

Sovereign AI-as-a-service / SLMs: zero-trust + tiered architecture (Tier-1 private on-prem/VPC SLMs fine-tuned on enterprise data; Tier-2 frontier models via policy-enforcing inferencing gateway). $150M strategic investment in Sarvam opens Indian sovereign-AI market; SLM-training = "another engineering-services wave."
AI IP / platforms: AI Force 2.2 (VS Code plugin, multimodal, long-term memory, AWS-native), Agent Store, AI Force for Oracle; deployed across 92 client accounts; 23 industry AI solutions.

Partnerships: Red Hat (AI Factory), Google Cloud (dedicated Gemini enterprise BU + autonomous finance platform), Intel + Google Cloud AI Innovation Zones (Santa Clara, Chennai), OpenAI Trusted Access for Cyber, AWS AI Services Competency, Dell/HPE partner-of-the-year, MetLife Stadium AI partner (FIFA 2026 final venue).
margins & cost dynamics: Reported EBIT margin walk QoQ (JFM'26 16.5% → AMJ'26 16.9%, +39bps): +70bps lower restructuring, +20bps PDD benefit, +60bps forex; −110bps seasonality (annual productivity give-backs + ERS decline).
Restructuring 62bps drag in Q1; ex-restructuring margin 17.5% (vs 17.7% prior Q).

Guidance embeds ~40–50bps restructuring cost for FY27. Strategy = "superior growth at stable margins"; won't compromise mega-deal margins (risk-management/execution rigor). Gross margin/employee expected to rise with revenue/employee, but mgmt "will not hesitate to invest" through the AI inflection.
capex / expansion (watch slippage) — ai: Entering the AI-datacenter business: strategic investment of up to INR3,500 crore (initial), with a long-term ambition to scale to 50MW of capacity.

INR3,500cr is NOT the cost of 50MW — mgmt explicit: it funds "a fraction of that capacity" to get started; 50MW is the long-term vision. Full-stack 50MW at ~$60–80B/GW math implies ~INR30,000cr, but mgmt "don't expect to be anywhere near INR30,000cr."

Funding: won't sit entirely on balance sheet in one year; mix of partners (silicon/OEM vendors), committed client capacity, GPUs financed against contracted demand, and equity+debt. Explicitly not at the expense of the payout policy.

Full-stack, not colo: "megawatt isn't the product, it's the anchor" — value is high-margin AI services (SLM-led, industry/vertical models) wrapped around capacity; drives outcome-based + managed-services contracts (some capacity consumed internally).

Demand backdrop: global DC demand to triple by 2030 (AI ~70% of growth), India even faster + one of the most supply-constrained DC markets; sovereign-data mandates require in-country workloads. Market "heavily GPU-starved… no ambiguity."
Client commitment: in advanced discussions to secure committed consumption "from day one." Next-tranche investment gated on delivery of the initial investment (disciplined, FCF-linked).
Note: separate $150M strategic investment in Sarvam (sovereign-AI stack) — distinct from the DC capex.
capital allocation: Interim dividend INR12/share (record date 17-Jul-26, pay 27-Jul-26); LTM dividend INR60/share = 93.2% payout of net income. (Prior-year board policy: return ≥75% of net income.)
AI-datacenter capex explicitly ring-fenced from the payout policy; funded via FCF + partner/debt mix, disciplined and staged.
Acquisitions: Jaspersoft (completed), CTG (pending), Sarvam ($150M strategic stake).
risks & watch-items: Two large US telcos — sharp discretionary-spend cuts; already flagged last quarter, now playing through ERS (Tech/Telecom/Media) in subsequent quarters.

Healthcare / Life Sciences — structural drag: off a ~$500M run-rate, gradual decline over 8–9 quarters; medical-device regulatory work ended and wasn't refilled; US healthcare sector "heavily stressed" (most of the vertical's revenue is US).

AI price deflation — AI-disrupted/commoditised services being optimised away; TCV-per-deal pressure; token-cost economics (costs may fall but total token consumption/cost rises → need economic tiered/SLM model).

Datacenter execution / tenancy risk — analyst pushback on ROIC/tenancy if the compute-demand cycle turns (100GW of announced AI-DC pipeline; SpaceX/Meta leasing compute); mgmt counters market is "heavily GPU-starved," 50MW is a tiny fraction of need.
Guidance conservatism — held 1–4% despite record bookings; macro unchanged since March; directional update only after Q2.
New Labor Code one-time EPS impact; DSO up 2 days.
management quality / tone: Confident and specific on AI strategy (five pillars, named deals, hard AI-revenue numbers); disciplined on capital ("won't correlate INR3,500cr with 50MW," FCF-gated, payout-protected).
Transparent on idiosyncratic weakness (named two-telco cuts, healthcare structural drag) rather than glossing.
Pragmatic on guidance — deliberately conservative given only one quarter in and unchanged macro; measured on mega-deal contribution timing (Apr-2027 steady state).
non-obvious takeaways: The AI-datacenter move is a business-model inflection — a services company building infrastructure, which mgmt frames as a reversal of the cloud/digital cycle (then you partnered hyperscalers; now private/sovereign SLM stacks require owning the full stack). Watch capital discipline vs. scope creep toward 50MW.
"Megawatt is the anchor, not the product" — the DC play is really a wrapper to lock in high-margin managed-services/outcome-based contracts and internal consumption, not a colo/capacity land-grab.
Sovereign-AI/SLM thesis reframes AI deflation as an engineering-services tailwind (data work + model training per client) rather than a pure headwind.
Record Q1 bookings + a separately-announced mega deal, yet guidance untouched — signals mgmt sees near-term revenue governed by seasonality/give-backs and the telco/healthcare drag, not order intake.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.

hero.oneLiner: HCLTech is a preferred digital transformation partner to Global 2000 enterprises, with a differentiated, future-ready full-stack portfolio spanning engineering, digital, cloud, AI and software delivered across 60 countries.
